biological.citation: Variants in RHOBTB2 associated with cancer and rare developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (PMID: 39736890)
biological.summary: RHOBTB2 is a Rho GTPase subfamily member and known tumor suppressor. BTB domain variants result in decreased proteasomal degradation and DEE onset, while GTPase domain variants cause variable neurodevelopmental symptoms without impairing degradation. Accumulation of RHOBTB2 in neural tissues contributes to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy pathogenesis.

biological.citation: RHOBTB2 enhances cell proliferation of acute myeloid leukemia by modulating Hippo-YAP1 signaling and dependent of KLHL13 (PMID: 41107424)
biological.summary: RHOBTB2 is markedly upregulated in AML and correlates with unfavorable prognosis. RHOBTB2 directly interacts with KLHL13 and stabilizes it by inhibiting proteasomal degradation, thereby modulating the Hippo-YAP1 signaling pathway to enhance AML cell proliferation and migration while suppressing apoptosis.

biological.citation: Ectopic expression of RhoBTB2 inhibits migration and invasion of human breast cancer cells (PMID: 20930524)
biological.summary: Ectopic RHOBTB2 expression in MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-435 breast cancer cells dose-dependently inhibits migration and invasion by upregulating the metastasis suppressor BRMS1 and decreasing phosphorylation of ezrin and Akt2, key regulators of cancer cell motility.

biological.citation: The atypical Rho GTPase RhoBTB2 is required for expression of the chemokine CXCL14 in normal and cancerous epithelial cells (PMID: 18762809)
biological.summary: Loss of RHOBTB2 via RNA interference in primary human epithelial cells results in downregulation of CXCL14, a chemokine controlling leukocyte migration and angiogenesis. RHOBTB2 reintroduction restores CXCL14 secretion, identifying CXCL14 as a direct gene target of RHOBTB2.

biological.citation: RhoBTB2 (DBC2) is a mitotic E2F1 target gene with a novel role in apoptosis (PMID: 18039672)
biological.summary: RHOBTB2 is a direct transcriptional target of E2F1. RHOBTB2 is upregulated during mitosis and drug-induced apoptosis in an E2F1-dependent manner. Knockdown of RHOBTB2 delays drug-induced apoptosis, indicating roles in both cell cycle progression and apoptosis regulation.

biological.citation: Mutant-specific dysfunction of RHOBTB2 impairs mitochondrial function and Na(+)/K(+)-ATPase levels in a cell model (PMID: 41478322)
biological.summary: Disease-associated RHOBTB2 mutants show distinct phenotypes: BTB domain hotspot mutants (R461H, R485C, R489Q) accumulate in nucleus and mitochondria, while GTPase-domain mutants (D92H, W217C) show normal protein levels. Mutant RHOBTB2 reduces Na+/K+-ATPase via lysosome-dependent degradation and impairs mitochondrial respiration, linking mutant RHOBTB2 to seizure susceptibility through ion homeostasis disruption.

biological.citation: Missense Variants in RHOBTB2 Cause a Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy in Humans, and Altered Levels Cause Neurological Defects in Drosophila (PMID: 29276004)
biological.summary: De novo BTB-domain missense variants in RHOBTB2 cause early-onset epilepsy, intellectual disability, microcephaly, and movement disorders in 10 patients. Mutant RHOBTB2 is more abundant due to impaired proteasomal degradation. In Drosophila, elevated RhoBTB levels cause seizure susceptibility and severe locomotor defects, while RhoBTB knockdown in dendritic arborization neurons decreases dendrite number, suggesting a role in dendritic development.

biological.citation: Downregulated RhoBTB2 expression contributes to poor outcome in osteosarcoma patients (PMID: 23777252)
biological.summary: RhoBTB2 protein is weakly expressed in osteosarcoma specimens but highly expressed in normal bone tissue. RhoBTB2 expression correlates with primary location and local recurrence. Overexpression of RHOBTB2 in HOS osteosarcoma cells results in G1 phase arrest and apoptosis induction.

biological.citation: RhoBTB2 is a substrate of the mammalian Cul3 ubiquitin ligase complex (PMID: 15107402)
biological.summary: RHOBTB2 binds to the ubiquitin ligase scaffold Cul3 via its first BTB domain and is a substrate for Cul3-based ubiquitin ligase complexes. A lung cancer-associated RHOBTB2 missense mutant cannot bind Cul3 and is not regulated by the ubiquitin/proteasome system, resulting in increased protein levels. This suggests RHOBTB2 functions as a tumor suppressor by recruiting proteins to Cul3 ubiquitin ligase for degradation.

biological.citation: Hsp90-dependent assembly of the DBC2/RhoBTB2-Cullin3 E3-ligase complex (PMID: 24608665)
biological.summary: RHOBTB2 (DBC2) is a client protein of the Hsp90 chaperone machine. RHOBTB2 retains capacity to bind GTP, and GTP binding is modulated by the Hsp90 ATPase cycle. Assembly of RHOBTB2-Cullin3-COP9 E3 ligase complexes is Hsp90-dependent, revealing a new paradigm for Hsp90-modulated assembly of Cul3/RHOBTB2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complexes.
